judgment_text:
Prayer in CRP No. 1512 of 2026

Prayer in CRP No. 1511 of 2026

COMMON ORDER

1. Challenging the impugned orders passed in I.A. Nos. 4 of 2024 and 7 of 2025 in O.S. No. 2236 of 2019 by the learned VI Additional Judge, City Civil Court, Chennai, the Revision Petitioner/3rd defendant preferred this Civil Revision Petition.

2. Since the relief is claimed challenging the order passed by the trial Judge, notice to the respondents is dispensed with.

3. Before the trial court, the Revision Petitioner/3rd defendant filed applications to mark the document and also to file additional written statement. Both applications were dismissed by the trial Judge holding that to receive additional written statement is highly belated one and other documents, which he wanted to produce is not relevant to the proceedings.

4. Considering the fact that the Revision Petitioner is the bank and according to their objections stated before the trial court that already the property was auctioned on issuing notice to the third party as per SARFAESI proceedings and as on date, the suit property is not belong to 1st and 2nd defendants as alleged by the plaintiff So also, the alleged sale agreement between the parties is collusive one and not binding the auction proceedings. Therefore, to prove the same, they wanted to produce the document, but the trial Judge has not given such opportunity. If the opportunity is not given to the Revision Petitioner to produce those documents, it will lead to miscarriage of justice, since already the property was sold under SARFAESI proceedings. The reason assigned by the trial Judge as such is illegal and the same is liable to be set aside. Accordingly, the findings rendered in I.A. Nos. 4 of 2024 and 7 of 2025 in O.S. No. 2236 of 2019 passed by the VI Additional Judge, City Civil Court, Chennai is set aside. The Revision Petitioner is directed to file additional written statement and to adduce evidence. Accordingly, these Civil Revision Petitions are allowed. No costs. Consequently, connected civil miscellaneous petitions are closed.
